questions.question: An LP in variables $x_1,x_2\ge0$ has constraints of three kinds, all with positive right-hand sides: $\le$, $\ge$ and $=$. Before starting from $x_1=x_2=0$, which constraints receive an artificial variable?
options: The $\ge$ and $=$ constraints
Only the $=$ constraints
Only the $\ge$ constraints
All constraints, including $\le$

questions.question: The equation $x_1+2x_2=8$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) is temporarily written as $x_1+2x_2+R_1=8$ with artificial variable $R_1\ge0$. What does a solution with $R_1=3$ mean for the original equation?
options: It holds with 3 units of unused capacity
It fails: $x_1+2x_2$ is 5 instead of 8
It holds, since $R_1$ is a valid slack
It holds with an excess of 3 above 8

questions.question: An LP is rewritten with slack $s_1$ in a $\le$ row, surplus $S_2$ in a $\ge$ row and artificial variables $R_2$, $R_3$ in the $\ge$ and $=$ rows. Which statement about these added variables is correct?
options: All four measure how far a constraint is from binding
$s_1$ and $S_2$ record real room; $R_2,R_3$ have no meaning
$R_2,R_3$ measure unused resources, like the slack $s_1$
$S_2$ and $R_2$ cancel, so only one of them is needed

questions.question: The constraint $4x_1+x_2\ge8$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) is to be written with surplus $S_1\ge0$ and artificial $R_1\ge0$. Which equation is correct?
The equation $x_1-2x_2=-4$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) is to receive an artificial variable $R\ge0$ that starts at the right-hand side while $x_1=x_2=0$. What must be done first?
options: Multiply by $-1$: $-x_1+2x_2+R=4$
Add it directly: $x_1-2x_2+R=-4$
Use a slack: $x_1-2x_2+s=-4$
Add a surplus: $x_1-2x_2-S+R=-4$

questions.question: A modeller adds artificial variables $R_i\ge0$ to the $=$ rows of an LP and then simply solves the original objective with the $R_i$ still in the constraints, at zero cost. What goes wrong?
options: Nothing, since an optimal solution always has every $R_i=0$
The model becomes infeasible, since the $R_i$ conflict
The equations can be met via $R_i>0$, loosening the model
The optimal value stays equal, only the solution changes

questions.question: Constraints $2x_1+3x_2=6$ and $3x_1-x_2\ge4$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) are written as $2x_1+3x_2+R_1=6$ and $3x_1-x_2-S_1+R_2=4$. For which point $(x_1,x_2)$ can both artificial variables be 0?

An LP with $x_1,x_2\ge0$ has the constraints $x_1+x_2\le10$, $x_1-x_2\ge2$, $x_1+2x_2=8$, $-x_1-x_2\le-3$, $2x_1-x_2\ge-4$ and $-x_1+x_2\ge-5$. After making every right-hand side nonnegative, how many artificial variables are needed?

An equality constraint $x_1+x_2=5$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) needs a variable that can start at 5 when $x_1=x_2=0$. Why is a slack $s\ge0$, as in $x_1+x_2+s=5$, not acceptable here, while an artificial $R$ is?
options: A slack stays in the model and turns $=5$ into $\le5$
A slack would start at $-5$, which breaks $s\ge0$
A slack has a positive cost, an artificial a zero cost
A slack can only be used for $\ge$ constraints

questions.question: The constraint $x_1-x_2\ge0$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) must be prepared for a start at $x_1=x_2=0$. Is an artificial variable needed?
options: No: as $-x_1+x_2\le0$ it takes a slack starting at 0
Yes: every $\ge$ constraint needs an artificial variable
Yes: the surplus starts at a negative value at $x=0$
No: the constraint can be dropped, as $x=0$ satisfies it

questions.question: An auxiliary problem for artificial variables $R_1,R_2\ge0$ must drive both to zero. A student proposes to minimize $R_1-R_2$ instead of $R_1+R_2$. Why does this fail?
options: It is unbounded, since $R_1$ can grow without limit
It makes the starting point $R_1=b_1$, $R_2=b_2$ infeasible
It rewards a large $R_2$, so $R_2$ need not reach 0
It works equally well, as both are linear objectives

questions.question: Rows $2x_1+3x_2+R_1=6$ and $3x_1-x_2-S_1+R_2=4$ (all variables $\ge0$) come from $2x_1+3x_2=6$ and $3x_1-x_2\ge4$. With $x=(2,0)$ fixed and $S_1,R_1,R_2$ free to choose, what is the smallest possible $R_1+R_2$?

An LP maximizes $x_1+x_2$ s.t. $2x_1+3x_2=6$, $3x_1-x_2\ge4$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Minimizing $R_1+R_2$ in the rewritten rows reaches $R_1=R_2=0$ at $x=(2,\frac{2}{3})$. What does this point tell us about the original LP?
options: It is feasible, though $(3,0)$ is better, so it is not optimal
It is optimal, since the artificials reached the best value 0
It is infeasible, since the surplus $S_1=\frac{4}{3}$ is positive
It is feasible, and its value $\frac{8}{3}$ bounds the optimum above
